title: Chapter 56: She Who Cannot Be Named
html:
There were too many missing clues to draw a conclusion. Chen Ge restored the three chairs and surveyed the studio. The mirrored wall made the room feel larger and emptier than it was.

This place is too clean. Someone must have cleaned it more than once recently.

Not a scrap of rubbish remained on the floor, which was bad news. Someone has disturbed the scene already. I only hope they didn’t throw out the red dancing shoes.

He moved from the mirrors to a corner where certificates and awards covered the wall. Among them hung what appeared to be a results sheet. On closer inspection, he found that the winner’s name had been blacked out with marker.

A list without the winner?

Chen Ge found all of the girls’ names, including Qian Yujiao, on the list, but he could not find Zhang Ya.

A photograph nearby caught his attention. It had originally shown six people. Five girls embraced and smiled at the camera, while the sixth stood apart in one corner. Someone had cut her from the print; without the tips of her snow-white dancing shoes still visible at the edge, Chen Ge would have assumed it was a picture of only five girls.

These are all portraits and small group shots. Why isn’t there a photograph of the whole class?

He photographed the wall, then followed it to an unmarked room. Curiosity drew him inside.

The cramped space held a desk, a dresser, and a single bed.

This looks like the teacher’s office, but why is there a bed? Did the teacher work nights?

He searched the room thoroughly for the red dancing shoes. The dresser was empty, and the desk drawers contained only photocopied award certificates.

The dance students must have been talented to win so many prizes.Chen Ge examined several certificates. One listed Qian Yujiao’s group. Swan Lake Citywide Ballet Group Competition Champion. That qualified them for the provincial competition.

This certificate had not been displayed outside. More curiously, the winning group should have listed six members, but someone had once again blacked out the final name.

It’s the same as the result list.

After one final search, Chen Ge left empty-handed. His heart lurched as he opened the door. The three chairs had abandoned their places by the mirrors and gathered closer to the office.

It has started again!

He forced himself to ignore them and hurried on. If he found nothing within three minutes, he would leave the Arts Activities Center. By the light of his phone, he crossed to the far end of the studio and found a door marked GIRLS’ DRESSING ROOM.

According to the rumors, girls’ bathrooms and dressing rooms have the strongest Yin energy in any school. I need to be extra careful.

He eased the door open. Steel lockers lined both walls, and a long wooden bench occupied the center.

So this is what the girls’ dressing room looks like.

He had never entered one before. Leaving the door half-open, he stepped inside and opened the nearest locker. A school uniform lay on the top shelf. Its design was more refined than the uniforms worn at public schools.

The skirt would barely reach my knees. Isn’t that a little short?

The uniform’s pockets were empty. On a lower shelf sat a pair of white dancing shoes.

Wrong color. These aren’t the ones I’m looking for.

As he closed the locker, he noticed a small name card above its lock. That should make this easier.

He checked each name by phone light but found no Zhang Ya. One unmarked locker stood alone in the corner, separated from all the others.

Its owner must have been ostracized.He opened it. Apart from a dirty ballet dress on the top shelf, the locker appeared empty.

No name, set apart from the rest… Who did this belong to?He already suspected the answer. Beneath the dress he found five boxes of candy, their contents long since spoiled.

Were these gifts?He laid the dress on the wooden bench and examined the boxes. Each had been wrapped by hand and labeled with a different girl’s name, all in the same handwriting.

She must have prepared these as gifts.

Beneath the final box lay a photograph—the complete version of the mutilated picture outside. A note on the back read, “Congratulations to Room 414 on qualifying for the provincial competition.” Six girls appeared on the front.

Five celebrated together on the right. The sixth stood a small but unmistakable distance apart. Nearly 1.7 meters tall, she had the grace and purity of Swan Lake’s heroine. Even in a still image, she seemed set apart from the others.

“Could this be Zhang Ya?” Chen Ge muttered. He could not reconcile the girl in the picture with the cruel, vicious Red Specter.

He had spoken Zhang Ya’s name without thinking. At once, every locker began to creak and rattle as though something inside were straining to burst free. Then came a relentless pounding from beyond the door, as if someone were trying to force their way in.

“Who is it?”

Chen Ge shoved the photograph into his pocket and tightened his grip on the mallet. Through the half-open door, he saw that the three chairs had formed a barricade across the entrance.

“Do you really think I won’t smash you to pieces?” Cold sweat soaked his back, but he advanced with the mallet raised. The dressing room had no other exit. If he did not clear a path now, his situation would only worsen.

His gaze swept the studio as he planned his escape. Then it reached the mirrored wall, and his legs stopped.

The mirrors reflected the dance studio exactly as it was—with one difference. Three girls sat in the three wooden chairs.
